source.title: Compound File Binary File Format
source.authority_boundary: The byte-pinned Microsoft DOCX and its exact normalized source rows are authoritative. The rules below are labeled project interpretations used by the strict inventory and do not replace the selected source text.

selected_sections.title: Compound File Sector Numbers and Types
project_interpretations: Regular chain pointers are at most MAXREGSECT; the final pointer is ENDOFCHAIN.
No sector belongs to more than one chain and no chain contains a cycle.
The actual sector count matches the size specified for a chain.
Unallocated sectors are represented by FREESECT in the FAT.

selected_sections.title: Compound File Header
project_interpretations: The signature is D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1 and the header CLSID is zero.
Minor Version SHOULD be 0x003E for Major Version 3 or 4.
Major Version is 3 or 4, with sector shifts 9 or 12 respectively.
Byte Order is 0xFFFE, Mini Sector Shift is 6, and the six reserved bytes are zero.
Mini Stream Cutoff Size is 0x00001000.
The version 4 header-sector padding after byte 512 is zero.

selected_sections.title: FAT, Mini FAT, and DIFAT Sectors
project_interpretations: Every physical sector is represented by the FAT, including free sectors.
FAT entries beyond physical end-of-file are FREESECT.
Mini-sector offsets are mini-sector number multiplied by 64 within the mini stream.
The mini stream is a normal FAT chain rooted by directory stream ID 0.
The final DIFAT link is ENDOFCHAIN and FAT/DIFAT allocation markers match their sector roles.

selected_sections.title: Directory Entries and Sibling Trees
project_interpretations: Directory stream ID 0 is the root storage entry and its name is Root Entry.
The root directory entry color is irrelevant because that entry has no siblings.
Each sibling-tree root is black and two consecutive sibling nodes are not both red.
Sibling names are unique and sorted by UTF-16 name length, then simple uppercase code units.
The MS-CFB sibling-tree rules do not impose the classical equal-black-height invariant.
Streams below the 4096-byte cutoff use mini FAT; larger streams use FAT.
Unused directory entries are zero except for three NOSTREAM sibling/child pointers.

selected_sections.title: User-Defined Data and Range Lock Sectors
project_interpretations: Application stream bytes are arbitrary and are not semantically validated by MS-CFB.
Each user-data chain has one directory entry and enough allocated bytes for its declared size.
The unused tail of a user-data sector SHOULD be zero, but a preservation inventory must retain observed nonzero tails.
When required above 2 GiB, the range-lock sector is FAT-allocated as ENDOFCHAIN and is not used by structural chains.

strict_inventory_policy: For this evidence profile, Minor Version is required to be the recommended 0x003E observed in all captured exports.
User-data chains are required to use the minimum whole-sector count and terminate immediately; this is stricter than the source requirement of enough allocated bytes and prevents hidden surplus data.
Every supplied physical byte and every mini-stream allocation unit is hashed, including application bytes and allocation slack; hashing does not assign application semantics.
